key_insight: AUTOPILOT-VQA introduces a benchmark focused on incident-centric dashcam understanding, making it easier to test whether vision-language models can reason about safety-critical driving events rather than just general scenes. The paper highlights a key gap: strong multimodal models still need rigorous evaluation on real-world driving incidents.
problem_solved: Existing autonomous driving benchmarks often emphasize general scene understanding, but they do not adequately measure how well models interpret and reason about safety-critical incidents in dashcam video.
method: Create an incident-centric visual question answering benchmark for dashcam video understanding.
Frame evaluation around safety-relevant questions that require reasoning about what happened, why it matters, and what could happen next.
Use the benchmark to compare vision-language and multimodal models on incident understanding performance.
impact: This work gives researchers and practitioners a more realistic way to evaluate multimodal systems for autonomous driving and safety applications. It can help identify model weaknesses before deployment in high-stakes environments.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing dashcam video -> incident question -> model answer -> benchmark score

paper_title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
paper_authors: Siddharth Damodharan, Radhika Gupta, Ali Alshami, Ryan Rabinowitz, Jugal Kalita
